welcome.title: Welcome to the Creature Planner
welcome.body: Three tabs up top. Summon plans new summons, Awaken Rush takes creatures to level 70 so they can awaken, and Prestige Loop farms prestige tokens with a stable party. This tour walks whichever one you’re on.

summonHeader.title: Plan your next summons
summonHeader.body: Add the creatures you want to summon and the planner totals up everything you still need to gather for them — flagging blockers like skill gates.

summonOrder.title: Your summon order
summonOrder.body: Your queue of summons, numbered in the order to tackle them — #1 is “do this now”. Re-sort by step order, readiness, or name; add more with the + row; and pick any row to focus its plan on the right.

summonFocus.title: The focused creature
summonFocus.body: The creature you’re on: its time-to-ready, the items it still needs (passive supply marked separately from hands-on work), and ways to speed those gathers up.

summonViews.title: Two ways to view it
summonViews.body: Plan (what you’ve seen so far) walks each creature in order. All materials — switching to it now — is the full gather list across every summon, grouped by source.

summonMaterials.title: Everything to gather
summonMaterials.body: Every material your queued summons need, pooled and grouped by where it comes from — your one shopping list. Switch back to Plan anytime to work creature-by-creature.

awakenQueue.title: Your awaken queue
awakenQueue.body: Add the unawakened creatures you want to take to level 70. One creature shows a detailed plan; add several and the planner optimizes them together as a party.

awakenBoosters.title: Optional boosters
awakenBoosters.body: Awakened creatures you allow here can escort the queue and speed it up, without being leveled themselves.

awakenStrategy.title: Strategy
awakenStrategy.body: Hands-free gives each creature a stable route with few reassignments — set it and check back in hours. Optimal coordinates the whole queue for the fastest overall finish, at the cost of more swaps.

awakenExpeditions.title: Expeditions
awakenExpeditions.body: Which expeditions the planner may route through, and how many are in scope. Narrow them to match what you actually run.

awakenFocus.title: Your plan
awakenFocus.body: The fastest expedition route to level 70 appears here, with when each creature lands.

awakenViews.title: Timeline or Steps
awakenViews.body: Timeline is a Gantt of the whole queue across time; Steps breaks the same plan into an ordered, wave-by-wave checklist.

awakenTimeline.title: Reading the timeline
awakenTimeline.body: Hold ⌘/Ctrl and scroll to zoom in and out; hold Shift and scroll to pan across time. The +/− buttons zoom too, and reset returns to the default.

awakenSetup.title: Push it to Expeditions
awakenSetup.body: View Initial Setup in Expeditions writes the plan’s first wave of parties into your Expeditions page, ready to apply in-game.

loopRoster.title: Loop roster
loopRoster.body: The awakened creatures that run the loop. After you calculate, each row shows its role — {anchor}, {booster}, or {climber}.

loopCadence.title: Check-in cadence
loopCadence.body: {cadence} The table shows tokens per day for each cadence so you can compare at a glance.

loopExpeditions.title: Expeditions
loopExpeditions.body: Which expeditions the loop may route through, and how many are in scope. Narrow them to match what you actually run.

loopHero.title: Your payoff
loopHero.body: Prestige tokens per day from this setup. {prestige} Open “Learn more” for how the set-and-leave strategy works.

loopTabs.title: Setup & Levels
loopTabs.body: Setup is the party assignment to apply right now. Levels charts each creature across check-ins — {levelChart}

playerLevel.headline: Raise low skills → +{levels} player level | Raise low skills → +{levels} player levels

awakenPoint.short: Earned when you awaken a creature. Spend it on any node in the awaken tree.
awakenPoint.long: Awakening a creature earns exactly one awaken point. The tree is job-based (e.g. Mining Duration, Chopping XP) rather than creature-based, so a point can go toward whichever job upgrade helps you most — it is never tied to a specific creature.

sanctuarySeat.short: A deployment slot. Seating an awakened creature lifts a job tier and speeds those gathers.
sanctuarySeat.long: A creature must be awakened before it can take a Sanctuary seat or act as a helper. Once seated, it raises the tier of a gather job, shortening every remaining gather for that job downstream.

checkIn.short: A return visit where you collect prestige tokens and re-form your parties.
checkIn.long: The prestige loop assumes you step away and come back on a fixed schedule. Each check-in is one of those returns: you bank the tokens earned since the last visit and the planner re-assigns parties for the next stretch.

cadence.short: How often you return — every 12h, 24h, etc. It changes how the loop is optimized.
cadence.long: Cadence sets the length of each unattended stretch. Shorter cadences let creatures prestige and be re-formed more often; longer cadences waste more time once creatures max out between visits.

prestige.short: When a creature hits the level cap, it resets to level 1 and earns a prestige token.
prestige.long: Prestiging is the loop’s payout: a creature that reaches the cap resets and yields a token. The whole planner is tuned to maximize how many of these resets happen per day across your roster.

rosterRoleAnchor.short: One of your strongest creatures, parked at level 120 to speed up its party. It never prestiges, so it earns no tokens itself.

rosterRoleBooster.short: Not a creature you pick — a Leveling creature that has reached level 120 and is boosting its party until it gets prestiged at the next check-in.

rosterRoleClimber.short: A creature climbing toward level 120. When it maxes out it prestiges for a token, then starts over.

levelChart.short: Each line is a creature’s level across check-ins. A line dropping back to 1 is a prestige reset.
levelChart.long: The Levels view plots every creature in an expedition’s party over time. A line that climbs toward the cap and then drops back to level 1 is a prestige — that reset is the moment a token was earned. Anchors stay flat near the top because they never reset.
